who: Christopher F. Jones, historian of energy and environment at Arizona State University; PhD Pennsylvania, History and Sociology of Science, 2009.

evidence.says: ASU identifies Christopher Jones as professor of history, author of Routes of Power, with a Pennsylvania PhD in History and Sociology of Science (2009).
Authority for Christopher F. Jones identifies the author of Routes of Power as a historian teaching at Arizona State University.
Chris Jones is the author of Eclipse of Empire? and a history lecturer at the University of Canterbury.
Christopher Prestige Jones is a Harvard professor of classics and history specializing in imperial Greek and Roman literature and history.

notes: The ASU affiliation, doctoral institution and energy-history publications identify Christopher F. Jones; the other two candidates have different affiliations and fields.

who: Pablo F. Gómez, historian of medicine and Latin America at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD Vanderbilt, 2010.

evidence.says: Wisconsin lists Pablo F. Gómez as professor of history and the history of medicine, with a Vanderbilt PhD in History of Medicine and Latin American History (2010).
The history department announced his appointment as assistant professor in November 2012, identifying the same Vanderbilt doctorate.
Authority for Pablo F. Gómez cites The Experiential Caribbean and its acknowledgment of Wisconsin–Madison’s Department of Medical History and Bioethics.

notes: Candidate affiliation, field, publication and doctoral institution agree; the Wisconsin appointment predates the listed dissertations.

who: Ute Frevert, historian of modern Germany; Yale professor of German history, 2003–2007; PhD Bielefeld, 1982.

evidence.says: Her institutional CV records a Bielefeld PhD (1982), the Yale professorship in German history (2003–2007), and a Max Planck directorship (2008–2024).
The candidate item identifies historian Ute Frevert, lists Yale as an employer and Bielefeld doctoral education, and carries LC identifier n85127822.

notes: Name, Yale appointment and German-history field establish the match. Listed dissertation completions in 2008–2013 postdate her Yale appointment; the CV alone does not verify each supervision.

who: Charters Wynn, historian of Soviet politics and labor at Texas at Austin since 1990; PhD Stanford, 1987.

evidence.says: His CV records the Stanford history PhD (1987), Texas appointments since 1990, and dissertation chairships for Travis Gray (2018), Andrew Straw (2017), Julie deGaffenried (2009), and Paul Hagenloh (1999).
Texas identifies Charters Wynn as a history professor studying Soviet political and labor history and author of Workers, Strikes and Pogroms.
Authority for Charters Wynn cites his Workers, Strikes, and Pogroms (1992).

notes: The institutional CV directly corroborates all four listed student chairships, with a spelling variant for deGraffenried.

who: Norman Ingram, historian of modern France at Concordia since 1992 and adjunct at McGill, 2000–2010; PhD Edinburgh, 1988.

evidence.says: His faculty page gives Edinburgh doctoral training and a February 1988 viva, Concordia appointment in 1992 and McGill adjunct appointment in 2000–2010; it lists supervisions of Mallet, Döderlein, Chagnon and Carle.
The authority identifies the author of The Politics of Dissent and The War Guilt Problem as Concordia’s professor of modern French history, appointed there in 1992.

notes: All four student names and both supervising institutions are corroborated. The faculty page dates Mallet and Döderlein to 2016 rather than the AHA’s 2017.

who: Grace Peña Delgado, historian of the U.S.–Mexico borderlands at California, Santa Cruz; PhD UCLA in American history, 2000.

evidence.says: UCSC identifies history professor Grace Peña Delgado, her UCLA PhD in American history (2000), and her research on North American borders.
The university repository identifies Grace Peña Delgado as advisor of Erik Bernardino’s 2021 history dissertation on labor and sex work in the California borderlands.
Authority for Grace Delgado cites In the Age of Exclusion (2000), whose title page identifies a UCLA PhD in History.

notes: LC-only candidate matches the doctoral institution and year; the repository directly corroborates a listed student under the fuller name.

who: Hal Bridges, historian of American social and intellectual history at California, Riverside, retiring in 1979; PhD Columbia.

evidence.says: The university memorial identifies Riverside history professor Hal Bridges, his Columbia doctorate in American social and intellectual history, his Civil War scholarship, and retirement in 1979.
The authority identifies Hal Bridges as author of Lee’s Maverick General and professor emeritus at California, Riverside.
H. R. (Herbert Rand) Bridges is an actor, also known as Rand Bridges, credited in Is It College Yet?

notes: LC-only Hal Bridges matches Riverside, the Columbia doctorate and American-history field; the alternative candidate is an actor.

who: Nancy J. Curtin, historian of Britain and Ireland at Fordham University, author of The United Irishmen.

evidence.says: Fordham names Nancy Curtin or Nancy J. Curtin as mentor for Pettinato, Conforti, Patterson and Flaten, matching the four listed students and dissertation subjects.
Authority for Nancy J. Curtin identifies the author of the 1994 United Irishmen book as an assistant professor of history at Fordham University.
Nancy A. Curtin is associated with the Department of Physiology at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School and Energetic Aspects of Muscle Contraction.

notes: Direct student matches establish Nancy J. Curtin rather than the physiology author. Fordham gives Conforti as 2011 and Patterson as 2000, differing from AHA dates; the supplied Wisconsin doctorate was not independently verified.
